documents.title: Statement on Guidance for the University of Pennsylvania Community on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The ISC statement sets general principles for all community members (disclose, verify, protect data) and says "Individual courses may have different or more narrow guidance", while telling instructors to give "clear guidelines". It sets no allow or ban rule for coursework itself, so it delegates.
documents.summary: University-wide Penn guidance on generative AI from Information Systems and Computing. It sets principles (transparency, accountability, bias, privacy, security, IP) for all members, and gives separate short sections for educators, students and researchers. Students are told to follow course rules and otherwise treat AI like help from another person.

units.why: The opening says "Penn embraces innovations like generative artificial intelligence" and sets the purpose of the guidelines; a statement of purpose and principles is P56. P02 was not chosen because the sentence frames the document rather than setting a rule for a course.

documents.unit: Center for Excellence in Teaching, Learning and Innovation (CETLI)
documents.title: Creating AI Policies
documents.stance_why: CETLI says "Penn does not have a standardized policy on student AI use, and each instructor is responsible for setting their own guidelines" and gives sample statements ranging from a full ban to open use with citation. It sets no stance itself and lists samples, so it delegates with tiers.
tiers: Sample: no generative AI (violation of Code of Academic Integrity)
Sample: AI with attribution (plagiarism if uncited)
Sample: open use with citation and student responsibility
Assignment samples: prohibited in-class on secure browser; AI not a scholarly source; required AI-Assisted Learning Disclosure
